documents.title: H&P - Admission - Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time seen: 21:40, ED bay 6
CHIEF COMPLAINT: cough and fever x 3 days, worsening shortness of breath today
HPI:
77M with cough productive of rust-colored sputum starting 3 days ago, then fevers to 38.9 at home, progressive dyspnea.
Today unable to walk to bathroom without stopping. Two episodes of vomiting this afternoon, poor oral intake since.
Prior antibiotic: leftover amoxicillin started at home yesterday; unclear number of doses. Pt cannot state dose or count of pills; daughter thinks 2 or 3 tablets total.
No chest pain, no hemoptysis, no orthopnea, no leg swelling. No recent travel. No sick contacts other than grandson with cold 1 wk ago.
Confused on arrival per daughter - knows name, not the month, repeating questions. Baseline independent, drives, manages own meds.
PMH:
COPD, mild, no home O2
HTN
Type 2 DM, diet controlled
BPH
Remote 40 pack-yr smoking hx, quit 15 yrs ago
HOME MEDS:
lisinopril 20 mg daily
amlodipine 5 mg daily
tiotropium inhaler daily
albuterol MDI prn
tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly
ASA 81 mg daily
ALLERGIES: no known drug allergies
SOCIAL: lives with wife in single-story home, daughter nearby. No etoh. No illicits.
ROS: positive for fever, chills, cough, dyspnea, nausea/vomiting, fatigue. Denies dysuria, diarrhea, rash, headache.
EXAM:
T 38.7, HR 104, respiratory rate 32 at triage, 30 at 4 hours. SpO2 93% on RA at triage.
Gen: ill-appearing elderly male, using accessory muscles, speaking in short phrases
HEENT: dry mucous membranes
Neck: no JVD, no adenopathy
Resp: crackles right base and right mid axilla, dullness to percussion right base, decreased breath sounds RLL, no wheeze
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no edema
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly
Neuro: oriented to person and place, not time. Follows commands. No focal deficit.
Skin: warm, no rash
LABS:
WBC 17.2 with 88% neutrophils, 6% bands; Hgb 13.4; Plt 212
Na 133, K 4.1, Cl 98, HCO3 22, BUN 34, Cr 1.3, glucose 188
Lactate 2.1, procalcitonin 4.8
Blood cultures x2 drawn 21:55. Sputum gram stain sent - gram positive diplococci reported 23:10.
Resp viral panel negative. HIV nonreactive.
IMAGING:
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion. No pneumothorax.
ASSESSMENT:
77M with community-acquired pneumonia, multilobar right sided, with confusion, tachypnea and elevated BUN. CURB-65 of 3 documented in the admitting note.
Severity supports inpatient management; no vasopressor or ventilatory requirement at present.
PLAN:
- Admit to medicine, telemetry bed
- Ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin; unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, so hold all PO abx and meds
- Ondansetron 4 mg IV q6h prn nausea
- O2 to keep SpO2 >92%; 1L NC placed overnight for SpO2 91% while sleeping
- Incentive spirometry q1h while awake, out of bed with assist
- Acetaminophen 650 mg q6h prn fever
- Hold lisinopril given Cr 1.3 and poor intake
- Trend WBC, BMP in AM; repeat lactate
- Delirium precautions, reorient, avoid sedatives
- Follow blood cultures; de-escalate when susceptibilities available
- Effusion small and non-loculated; no indication for thoracentesis now, reassess if enlarging or febrile persistently

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning - Medicine
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, seen 07:20
SUBJECTIVE:
Fever overnight to 38.4 at 02:10, responded to acetaminophen. Cough persists, sputum still discolored.
Vomited twice overnight, 23:50 and 05:15. Has not kept down water. Still unable to tolerate oral intake.
Less confused this morning - knows day and place. Daughter at bedside confirms closer to baseline.
RN notes 1L NC placed overnight for SpO2 91% while sleeping; remains on 1L NC this AM, comfortable.
OBJECTIVE:
T 37.9, HR 96, RR 24, SpO2 95% on 1L NC
Intake poor, urine output 900 mL/24h
Resp: crackles right base unchanged, dullness right base persists
CV: regular rate, no murmur. Abd soft. No edema.
LABS: WBC 14.1 (from 17.2), Na 134, BUN 28, Cr 1.2, lactate 1.4
Blood cultures: 1 of 2 bottles growing gram positive cocci in pairs, ID pending
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Multilobar CAP, CURB-65 of 3 on admission - clinically trending better, WBC down, mentation improved.
- Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin; unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, so all abx remain IV
- Likely pneumococcal given gram stain and preliminary culture; await final ID and susceptibilities
- Prior antibiotic: leftover amoxicillin started at home yesterday; unclear number of doses - noted, does not change current coverage
2. Hypoxemia - continue 1L NC, wean when SpO2 sustained >92% on RA including with ambulation
3. Nausea/vomiting - scheduled ondansetron 4 mg IV q8h, add IV pantoprazole, clear liquids as tolerated
4. Small right pleural effusion - no increase clinically, no drainage indicated, repeat imaging if worsening
5. AKI mild, improving - lisinopril remains on hold
6. Dispo: needs to keep down PO and off O2 before discharge. PT eval ordered.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD3 - Medicine
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD3, seen 07:45
SUBJECTIVE:
No fever in past 24h, Tmax 37.4 at 18:00 yesterday. No vomiting since 05:15 HD2.
Tolerated full clear liquids at dinner and a soft breakfast this AM without nausea.
Cough looser, less dyspnea, walked hallway with PT twice yesterday.
Fully oriented today, no further confusion.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.9, HR 82, RR 18, SpO2 94% on RA at rest, 93% after 200 ft walk
Weaned off NC at 22:30 last night, remained off overnight
Resp: scattered crackles right base, improved aeration, no wheeze
Abd soft, nontender. No edema.
LABS: WBC 9.8, Na 137, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, glucose 142
MICRO: blood cultures 1/2 bottles Strep pneumoniae, penicillin susceptible; sputum culture same organism
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Pneumococcal CAP, multilobar right sided, with bacteremia - responding well, afebrile >24h, WBC normalized.
- Now tolerating PO; de-escalate to oral amoxicillin per susceptibility after one more dose of ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily today
- Stop IV azithromycin today; total 3 days atypical coverage adequate given documented pneumococcus
- Plan total 7 days antibiotics counting inpatient days
2. Hypoxemia resolved - off O2 >12h, ambulatory sats acceptable, no further O2 orders
3. Small right pleural effusion - clinically stable, no respiratory compromise, no tap; PCP to arrange follow-up imaging
4. AKI resolved, Cr 1.0 - resume lisinopril 20 mg daily this AM
5. Nausea resolved - discontinue scheduled ondansetron, keep prn
6. PT: independent with cane on level surfaces, no further needs
7. Dispo: anticipate discharge home HD4 if remains afebrile and stable on PO abx overnight.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Community-Acquired Pneumonia - HD4
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit HD1, discharged HD4 at 13:40, disposition home with wife
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower and right middle lobe, with Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia
2. Small right pleural effusion, parapneumonic, no drainage required
3. Hypoxemic respiratory insufficiency, resolved
4. Acute delirium secondary to infection, resolved
5. Mild AKI, resolved
6. COPD, HTN, type 2 DM - stable
HOSPITAL COURSE:
77M presented with 3 days of fever and productive cough with confusion. Respiratory rate 32 at triage, 30 at 4 hours. SpO2 93% on RA at triage.
Prior antibiotic: leftover amoxicillin started at home yesterday; unclear number of doses.
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion. WBC 17.2, BUN 34, lactate 2.1.
CURB-65 of 3 documented in the admitting note; admitted to telemetry medicine bed.
Started on ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin; unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, so antibiotics and home meds kept IV or held.
1L NC placed overnight for SpO2 91% while sleeping on HD1; weaned off oxygen HD2 at 22:30 and remained on room air thereafter.
Blood cultures 1 of 2 bottles and sputum grew penicillin-susceptible S. pneumoniae. Azithromycin stopped HD3; narrowed to oral amoxicillin after final IV ceftriaxone dose HD3.
Nausea resolved HD3 with scheduled ondansetron; advanced to soft diet and tolerated. Mentation returned to baseline HD3. Cr improved 1.3 to 1.0, lisinopril resumed HD3.
Afebrile >48h at discharge, ambulating with cane, SpO2 94-95% on RA at rest and 93% with ambulation.
DISCHARGE VITALS: T 36.8, HR 78, RR 18, SpO2 95% RA
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
amoxicillin 1 g PO TID to complete through day 7 of total therapy
resume lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly, ASA 81 mg daily
tiotropium daily, albuterol MDI prn
ondansetron 4 mg PO q8h prn nausea, 6 tablets
acetaminophen 650 mg q6h prn
FOLLOW UP:
- PCP within 5 to 7 days for clinical recheck and to arrange repeat chest imaging in 6 to 8 weeks given multilobar disease and effusion
- Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination status to be addressed as outpatient
RETURN PRECAUTIONS: fever >38.3, worsening dyspnea, inability to keep down antibiotics, confusion, chest pain
Incentive spirometer to home, use hourly while awake. Increase activity daily.
